source_identity.title: Quasi-invariance of Gaussian measures for the 3d energy critical nonlinear Schrödinger equation

summary: Proposition A.9 is false under the endpoint-only Definition A.8. A smooth three-mode exact calculation and short-time continuity give a complete counterexample. An orbit-wide H1 bound restores refinement; conservation provides such a bound for compact initial families. No failure of Theorem 1.1 or Propositions 3.1/3.2 was established.

problems.title: An endpoint H1 bound need not survive refinement

claim.location: Definition A.8 and Proposition A.9, PDF p44
claim.text: For any A>delta>0, phi in H1 and an (A,delta)-partition of [-T,T] with H1 bounds only at existing left endpoints and Z norm <delta on each interval, every refinement remains an (A,delta)-partition with the same A and delta.

assumptions_checked: Defocusing quintic NLS on the three-torus
phi smooth and therefore in H1
No global-in-time H1 bound in Definition A.8
Single original interval allowed; no requirement that zero is an endpoint
Strict Z smallness arranged on a smooth short-time solution

check.analytic_argument: Smoothness makes H1 squared strictly increasing on a sufficiently small [-T,T]. Shrink T<1/2 so Z([-T,T])<delta. Original left endpoint -T has H1<A; refinement at T/2 creates a left endpoint with H1>A. All original conditions hold and the refined partition fails.
check.computation_kind: Exact Gaussian-integer convolution and separate SymPy 1.13.3 Laurent expansion; no time simulation

problems.result: Refutes the unrestricted local refinement statement in the acquired preprint.
counterevidence: Actual source image p44 confirms the endpoint-only hypothesis; no OCR-only issue.
The later T>=1 assumption in A.12 does not restrict A.9.
Energy is conserved but H1 itself need not be; exact derivatives verify this distinction.
Common refinement in A.12 can use a separately available uniform orbit bound. No core theorem failure is inferred from the false auxiliary wording.
No actual v3-to-journal text comparison or earlier report identifying this issue was recovered.

impact.dependency: A.12 Step1 pp45-46 cites A.9 for common refinement; p47 uses a common partition for higher regularity.
impact.bounded_conclusion: Local claim false. Since M+2H uniformly bounds the orbit and is bounded on compact H1 families, that application can satisfy the stronger premise independently. No demonstrated central damage.
impact.severity_reason: Supported local defect without demonstrated failure of a core conclusion; appendix location and repair length are not the basis for severity.

correction.statement: Add sup_{|t|<=T}||Phi(t)phi||H1<=A, or require a supremum bound on each original interval.
correction.proof: New endpoints then obey the same A bound, and restriction monotonicity gives every refined Z norm <delta.
correction.available_bound: ||Phi(t)phi||H1^2 <= M(phi)+2H(phi), with a finite uniform supremum on compact H1 sets.
correction.verification_status: Exact corrected refinement statement proved; no claim to have independently reconstructed every step of the entire revised appendix.

rejected_candidates.reason: Coarse interpolation already yields a summable negative frequency power; retaining low-frequency Sobolev weights yields p K^-1 and recovers the printed exponent. No defect assigned.

Selected summability and simultaneous exponent inequalities
Point-evaluation density and L1 transport isometry
